body:
_Migrated from issue #1195, filed 2026-07-28._

Two defects on the bulk-metadata path, both found while reviewing #1194 (the fix for #1169). Neither is a regression from that PR — this path has behaved this way all along — but #1194 fixed the single-book equivalent and left this one, so it's filed rather than half-done.

## 1. Bulk edits don't reconcile the catalog cache

`useBulkActions.setMetadata` (`frontend/src/lib/queries.ts`) posts to the same `/api/v1/books/<id>/metadata` endpoint as the single-book editor, but its success handler only invalidates `['books']`. It never touches the in-memory catalog snapshots.

What a user sees: select several books in the library, apply a tag/series/author change, scroll back later, and

- pages that weren't refetched still show the old author, tag or series;
- an author/tag/series listing, or the saved default view (#498), can still list books that no longer belong — or omit ones that now do;
- the retained `['adv-search']` pages have the same problem #1194 fixed for single edits.

The single-book path now handles all three via `applyBookEditToCache` plus a `removeQueries` on both key families.

## 2. The bulk mutation reports success even when every write failed

The same function wraps its fan-out in `Promise.allSettled` and returns the settled array. A settled array is a *fulfilled* promise regardless of what's in it, so react-query runs `onSuccess` and the UI reports a clean result even if every single request 403'd or 500'd.

## Why it isn't a one-line fix

`settle()` discards the fulfilled response bodies, so there's nothing to reconcile the cache *from*. Patching from the submitted fields instead would be wrong wherever the server normalises a value (author `,` → `|` escaping, series index coercion) or where an individual field write fails — the response is the only source of truth for what actually landed.

So the fix is to keep `{ id, data }` per fulfilled request, surface the rejected ones as a real partial-failure state, and then run each successful result through the same reconciliation the single-book path uses.

## Also missing

#1194's `['adv-search']` fix went in without a regression test of its own — the saved-default-filter ghost-card case is worth pinning while this path is being reworked.
title: Bulk metadata edits leave stale cards in the library, and report success even when every write failed
